Area.evidence_source: Prolonged drought was experienced by all of the farmers and reflected the uncertainty and lack of control over farming. As drought ensued, expenses increased (eg, buying water); consequently, workload increased, incidents of physical illness/injury increased, and financial security was threatened. As a consequence of drought and subsequent financial problems, a number of factors contributed to elevating distress among the farmers, including: change to family roles (spouses gaining employment and hence becoming absent from daily home routine and social interaction); feelings of uncertainty and incompetence around farm foreclosure, age, and not having skills to start other employment; loss of animals (selling or death of animals held in family for generations); increased costs (water, hay, transport); and increased farm expenditure (eg, cost of repairing machinery, threat of plant disease, regulation changes, and increased bank interest rates).
